lead: An optical fiber communication system carries information as light. A transmitter converts an electrical data signal into light, a glass fiber guides the light over distance, and a receiver converts the light back into an electrical signal. This idea exists because light in silica glass can travel far with low loss and can be switched very fast. Telephone trunks, internet backbones, cable TV, mobile towers and bank links use it. At 1550 nm, one fiber can carry many high-speed channels at once, which copper cables cannot do over long distances.

sections.h3: The three blocks of a fiber link

blocks.text: Every fiber link has three blocks: transmitter, fiber channel, receiver. The transmitter takes an electrical input, such as a digital bit stream from a router or an analog video signal from a cable head-end, and drives an optical source. The optical source is a light-emitting diode (LED) or a semiconductor laser. It emits light whose power follows the electrical signal. The fiber is a thin strand of silica glass with a core of higher refractive index and a cladding of lower refractive index. The core guides the light by total internal reflection; see 1.2. The receiver uses a photodetector, usually a PIN photodiode or an avalanche photodiode (APD), to convert incident light into current. A receiver circuit then amplifies and reshapes the signal to give the electrical output.

For a digital link, the source is switched between two light levels, often on and off, and the receiver decides each bit. For an analog link, the light power varies continuously with the input waveform, as in older cable TV distribution. The same three-block picture applies to both. The usual wavelength windows are named by their centre wavelengths: 850 nm for short multimode links, 1300 nm for metro links, and 1550 nm for long-haul links. Loss values for these windows belong to Unit 2.
Copper cable carries data as an electric current. Fiber carries data as light. This change gives several practical advantages.

items: Wide bandwidth. Light has a very high frequency, so the fiber channel can be modulated at very high rates. A single silica fiber can carry many gigabits per second, and with wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) it can carry many wavelengths at once. A copper pair has much lower bandwidth and loses more at high frequency.

Low loss. Silica glass is very transparent at the infrared windows. A signal can travel tens of kilometres before it needs amplification or regeneration. Copper suffers higher loss, so long copper links need repeaters frequently. Exact loss values are in Unit 2.

Immunity to electromagnetic interference. A fiber is a dielectric, not a conductor. It does not pick up currents from nearby power lines, lightning or electric motors. It also does not radiate, so it does not disturb other circuits. This helps near railway traction or heavy motors.
Small size and weight. One fiber is thinner than a human hair. A cable with many fibers has much less weight and bulk than a copper cable with the same capacity. This reduces duct and tower loading.
Electrical isolation. There is no metallic path between the two ends. This breaks ground loops and protects equipment from voltage differences and lightning surges.

Security. Light stays inside the core. Tapping a fiber is harder than tapping a copper pair, and a tap can change the loss and be detected. Fiber does not broadcast a signal that a nearby antenna can pick up.

blocks.text: These advantages explain why backbone routes, undersea cables, UPI payment data centres and mobile tower links use fiber.

sections.h3: Analog, digital, and the wavelength windows

blocks.text: At block level, an analog fiber link maps a continuous input voltage to a continuous light power. The receiver recovers a continuous voltage. Analog links are used for cable TV and some radio-over-fiber feeds. A digital fiber link maps bits to light pulses. The receiver samples each bit interval and decides whether the light was high or low. Almost all telephone and internet traffic is digital.

The link can also be described by its wavelength window. The window name is the centre wavelength of the source. 850 nm is used with short multimode links inside buildings. 1300 nm is used in metro links because it has low dispersion; dispersion is covered in Unit 2. 1550 nm is used in long-haul links because silica loss is lowest there. These are names only here; the loss and dispersion numbers come later.

blocks.where: L_dB is total fiber loss in decibels (dB); α is loss per kilometre in dB/km; z is fiber length in kilometres (km).
P_dBm is power in dBm; P_mW is power in milliwatts (mW).

blocks.text: Loss in dB adds with distance. The worked example uses these two relations.

examples.question: A 20 km fiber link uses a 1550 nm source and has fiber loss 0.2 dB/km. Find the total fiber loss. The input power is 1 mW. Find the output power in mW and in dBm.
steps: Identify the given values: loss per kilometre α = 0.2 dB/km and length z = 20 km.
Find total fiber loss: L_dB = α × z = 0.2 dB/km × 20 km = 4 dB.
Convert input power to dBm: P_in,dBm = 10 log₁₀(1 mW / 1 mW) = 10 log₁₀(1) = 0 dBm.
Subtract the loss: P_out,dBm = P_in,dBm − L_dB = 0 dBm − 4 dB = −4 dBm.
Convert back to milliwatts: P_out,mW = 1 mW × 10^(−4/10) = 0.398107 mW.
examples.answer: The total fiber loss is 4 dB, and with 1 mW input the output is −4 dBm, which is 0.398 mW (about 0.4 mW).
examples.check:
import math
z_km = 20.0
alpha_dB_per_km = 0.2
L_dB = alpha_dB_per_km * z_km
P_in_mW = 1.0
P_in_dBm = 10 * math.log10(P_in_mW)
P_out_dBm = P_in_dBm - L_dB
P_out_mW = 10 ** (P_out_dBm / 10)
print(L_dB)
print(P_in_dBm)
print(P_out_dBm)
print(round(P_out_mW, 3))

traps: Loss in dB adds with distance. Do not treat 0.2 dB/km as the total loss, and do not multiply powers in dB; add or subtract dB values.
dBm is an absolute power; dB is a ratio. A loss of 4 dB reduces 0 dBm to −4 dBm.
The source is the electrical-to-optical converter; the photodetector is the optical-to-electrical converter. Do not swap them.
850 nm, 1300 nm and 1550 nm are wavelength window names here. They are not loss values; loss numbers come in Unit 2.
Fiber immunity to EMI comes from being dielectric, not from carrying a larger current. A fiber carries no current along the data path.

quiz.q: Name the three blocks of a general optical fiber link.
What does a photodetector do in a fiber link?
quiz.a: It converts incident light into an electrical current, which the receiver circuit then amplifies and reshapes.

quiz.q: Why does a fiber link not pick up electromagnetic interference from a nearby motor?
quiz.a: The fiber is a dielectric and carries no current loop along the data path. Light is confined inside the core, so external electric and magnetic fields do not induce signal currents in the fiber.

quiz.q: A 12 km fiber has loss 0.25 dB/km. The input power is 2 mW. Find the total loss in dB and the output power in mW.
quiz.a: Total loss L_dB = 0.25 dB/km × 12 km = 3 dB. Input 2 mW is 10 log₁₀(2) = 3.0103 dBm. Output is 3.0103 − 3 = 0.0103 dBm. Output power = 2 mW × 10^(−3/10) = 1.002 mW.

quiz.q: Give two advantages of fiber over copper for a long backbone route.
quiz.a: Any two: wide bandwidth, low loss over long distance, immunity to electromagnetic interference, small size and weight, electrical isolation, and security.

quiz.q: A link uses a 1550 nm source and 20 km fiber with 0.2 dB/km. A technician says the output is 0.4 mW when the input is 1 mW. Is this consistent? Show dB reasoning.
quiz.a: Yes. Total loss = 0.2 dB/km × 20 km = 4 dB. Input 1 mW is 0 dBm. Output is 0 − 4 = −4 dBm. Converting back gives 1 mW × 10^(−4/10) = 0.398 mW, about 0.4 mW.

quiz.q: Why does a fiber link give electrical isolation between two buildings?
quiz.a: The signal crosses the gap as light inside a dielectric fiber. There is no metallic conductor joining the two ends, so ground potentials can differ without a ground loop and without carrying surge current between buildings.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern coherent links combine phase and amplitude modulation with digital signal processing, so a single 1550 nm carrier can carry hundreds of gigabits per second. Research systems use space-division multiplexing with multi-core fibers to push capacity higher. Silicon photonics puts modulators and detectors on a chip beside the fiber, which lowers cost for data centres. Search terms: coherent optical communication, silicon photonics, multi-core fiber, elastic optical network.
